question: Section 198 of the BNS corresponds to which IPC section?
explanation: s.198 re-enacts s.166 IPC: public servant disobeying law with intent to cause injury.

question: The punishment under Section 198 is—
options: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both
Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine
explanation: s.198: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or fine, or both.

question: Under Section 199(c), a public servant is punished for failing to record information given under—
explanation: s.199(c) refers to information given under sub-section (1) of section 173 of the BNSS, 2023 (the FIR provision, formerly CrPC s.154).

question: The punishment under Section 199 is—
options: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 6 months, up to 2 years, and fine
Rigorous imprisonment not less than 1 year, up to 3 years
explanation: s.199: rigorous imprisonment for not less than six months which may extend to two years, and fine.

question: Which of these offences is NOT listed in Section 199(c)?
explanation: The s.199(c) list is ss.64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 70, 71, 74, 76, 77, 79, 124, 143 and 144. Section 78 (stalking) is not in it.

question: Section 200 of the BNS applies to—
options: The person in charge of any hospital, public or private
Only doctors who treat the victim
explanation: s.200 covers whoever is in charge of a hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, State Government, local bodies or any other person.

question: The duty of hospitals to treat victims free of cost, enforced by Section 200, is found in—
explanation: s.200 punishes contravention of BNSS s.397 (formerly CrPC s.357C).

question: Under Section 201, a public servant who knowingly prepares an incorrect document to cause injury is punishable with—
options: Up to 1 year, or fine, or both
Up to 3 years, or fine, or both
explanation: s.201: imprisonment of either description up to three years, or fine, or both.

question: Section 201 applies to incorrect preparation or translation of—
explanation: s.201 covers any document or electronic record that the public servant is charged with preparing or translating.

question: Which punishment is NEWLY added to Section 202 (public servant unlawfully engaging in trade)?
explanation: s.202: simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both, or with community service. Community service was not in s.168 IPC.

question: Under Section 203, property unlawfully purchased by a public servant—
options: May be returned to the seller
Shall be auctioned again with his consent
Remains his after paying a fine
explanation: s.203: '...and the property, if purchased, shall be confiscated.'

question: Section 203 applies when the public servant buys the barred property—
options: In his own name, in another's name, jointly, or in shares with others
Only through a registered sale deed
explanation: s.203 covers purchases or bids 'either in his own name or in the name of another, or jointly, or in shares with others'.

question: The punishment for personating a public servant under Section 204 is—
options: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both
Not less than 6 months, up to 3 years, and fine
Up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹5,000
explanation: s.204: imprisonment of either description not less than six months, up to three years, and fine. Under s.170 IPC it was up to two years, or fine, or both.

question: Which is the only non-bailable offence in Chapter XII?
explanation: BNSS First Schedule: s.204 (personating a public servant) is cognizable and non-bailable; all others in the Chapter are bailable.

question: An essential ingredient of Section 204 that is NOT required under Section 205 is—
options: Doing or attempting an act under colour of the office
Intention that others believe he is a public servant
explanation: s.204 requires doing or attempting to do an act under colour of the pretended office; s.205 is complete on wearing the garb or carrying the token with the required intention or knowledge.

question: The maximum fine under Section 205 (wearing garb of a public servant) is—
explanation: s.205: up to three months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both. The IPC (s.171) fine was ₹200.

question: Which of these Chapter XII offences is non-cognizable?
explanation: ss.198, 200, 202 and 203 are non-cognizable; ss.199, 201, 204 and 205 are cognizable.

question: Offences under Chapter XII are triable by a Magistrate of the first class, EXCEPT—
options: ss.204 and 205, triable by any Magistrate
explanation: BNSS First Schedule: ss.198-203 are triable by a Magistrate of the first class; ss.204 and 205 by any Magistrate.
